Not a restatement of: Prior-result bullet 'unseen ~ seen, so the retrieved value is the type's procedure, not the scene': this idea plants scene bindings and predicts that the retrieval residual over the best static arm is the natural +17.2 plus a binding-created term that exists only when the environment gives no probe and only against a static artifact that names a test instead of enumerating; a 60-token rule removes the term under the testable regime and an observation-keyed table removes it under the untestable one. Digest card arxiv:2605.22219 (SGR-Bench: failures come from the wrong site-specific state; whether stored procedures or prior trajectories would fix it is untested): this idea builds the stored procedures (table and rule) and the trajectory retrieval, and claims that which of them is needed is decided by whether the wrong state is detectable before committing, a property it manipulates on the same games rather than names.
Changes made: P1: the stale-playbook loss under untestable is now a construction check (reported, not scored); the gate is S3 (per-game oracle names) vs S0, which measures compliance and can fail. P2: kept open; restated as swap penalties, TOST margin set above the +-8 half-width, type-agnostic clause (T0) added, and the self-recovery outcome named as a result rather than a design failure. P3 (headline): estimand changed to D(R3, untestable) with S1's inertness stated as construction; the retriever is estimated separately by a pre-registered same-kitchen hit rate and the R3o oracle-key arm, so a null is attributable; stated why P3 is not implied by P1. P4: margin above the half-width by doubling the swapped cell (complementary assignments, 528 pairs, floor +-8); permuted-table placebo cut as forced; raw R3 - S2 stated against the measured +17.2 natural residual and the manipulation that keeps the binding from adding to it named (enumeration); T1 clause added. P5 (seen-unseen gap) removed and all unseen cells cut; 'Not a restatement of' rewritten around the regime x artifact interaction. P6 (whole bank): W+/W- with the same-kitchen item's presence randomised within game, paired, sizes and floor stated. P7 -> P5 (cost): threshold moved above the mechanical step count; an upper bound (post-probe flailing) and an unswapped over-testing clause added so the estimand can come out against the hypothesis. Design: untestable regime made one-shot (silent commit) because an undetectable-but-reversible failure is probe-able by redundancy and would let a 30-token rule bypass the binding; baseline changed to static3 (best measured) with type-agnostic playbook arms retained as controls; goal-keyed k3 and k0 at q = .5 cut; arithmetic 17,036 episodes, ~11.5 h on two A100s plus one day of engineering. Short Hypothesis: the contradiction between 'residual over the best compiled artifact' and 'the table matches the query' resolved: the residual over the best static arm is the natural residual once the artifact enumerates the binding; the binding-created term appears only against a non-enumerating artifact under the untestable regime. The central claim was not softened: it still predicts a regime x artifact interaction with both halves scored on the same games, and the one-shot regime makes the risky half harder to pass, not easier.

Name: compile_the_statistics_not_the_trajectory
Title: What Retrieval Cannot Carry: Cross-Episode Location Statistics Compiled From the Bank Beat Retrieved Trajectories on Search-Bound Tasks
Short Hypothesis: A compiled artifact can hold a cross-episode aggregate (object -> receptacle location frequencies) that no set of k retrieved trajectories contains. On ALFWorld's search-bound types (pick-and-place, pick-two, look-at-in-light) a ~300-token, type-agnostic, cached cheatsheet compiled by rule from the expert pool recovers at least the Gate-0 retrieval gain on those types (~+10) over no memory at zero uncached prefill. Its value comes from aggregation, not coverage or scaffold: a coverage-matched table built from one sampled trajectory per object class loses most of it, a row-deranged table loses all of it, and the raw 80-item bank in context does not reproduce it unless the table compiled from those same items is added explicitly. Added to the best static arm (Measurement C's static3), the statistic removes the residual that k=3 retrieval keeps over it on the search-bound types (C: ~+9 there); it is not expected to touch the procedure-bound residual (+20..+27), which is reported as the scope boundary, not claimed.
Related Work: Measurement A on this node shows the retrieval gain is procedure-bound (unseen ~ seen) and smaller on the pick types (+15/+18/-5) than on heat/cool/clean (+39..+55). Measurement C (2026-09-09) finds the best static arm is static3 (3 fixed type-conditioned exemplars, ~430 tokens): static3 - k0 = +12.4, k3 - static3 = +17.2 with the residual concentrated on clean/heat/cool (+20..+27) and only +10..+12 on pick types, +4.8 on look-at (CI including 0); the type-agnostic six-procedure prompt is +9.5 over k0 and -20.1 under k3. No static arm in A or C carries anything a single trajectory cannot. Strategy graphs (2511.07800), verifier-promoted skill graphs (2512.23760), tutorials (2606.03951) and ICAL insight exemplars (2406.14596) compile trajectories but never at matched tokens against raw retrieval and never separate distillation from aggregation (G1); SkillEvolBench (2605.24117) finds raw reuse often beats distilled skills but its skills are procedures, not statistics. Dynamic Cheatsheet (2504.07952) accumulates insights at test time but never compares against retrieval of the raw episodes or varies the amount of experience compiled. An LLM-free ALFWorld agent (WCCIS 2026, 'Zero-Shot Embodied Decision Making with Structured Prior Knowledge') hand-builds object-location priors and shows they matter for a symbolic controller, but does not compile them from experience, vary aggregation depth, or compare with an LLM reader's retrieval. Object-search work in robotics (2607.00022 PerSim; 2603.05642 SymSearch) uses population-frequency placement priors, confirming the mechanism exists outside the agent-memory literature. Archived: compile_dont_retrieve (6.0) observed the read to be inert; here the compiled artifact is given content retrieval cannot have and that content is manipulated (depth at fixed coverage, derangement, no-experience prior). optimizer_substitutes_for_memory_scaffold (5.22) could not separate scaffold from content; the deranged-table placebo separates them by construction of the arm, not of the outcome.
Abstract: Agent-memory papers compare retrieval with no memory; the cheapest alternative, a fixed prompt compiled once from the same experience, is rarely run, and when compiled artifacts are studied their gain is not attributed. We isolate one thing compilation can do that per-query retrieval structurally cannot: aggregate across episodes. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B and the 1,465-item expert pool on this node, we compile by rule a ~300-token cheatsheet of object -> receptacle location frequencies (from the 'take X from Y' step of each trajectory) and place it, type-agnostically, in the instruction slot as a cached static prefix. On the 134 search-bound games (pick-and-place, pick-two, look-at-in-light) at 8 seeds we compare it, within one serving session, with no memory, k=3 retrieval, Measurement C's best static arm (static3), a depth ladder that varies how many trajectories per object class are aggregated at fixed coverage (1, 4, all), a token-matched deranged table, a same-format table written by Qwen3-32B without the bank, the raw 80-item bank in context (11k tokens, cached) with and without the table compiled from those same 80 items, and static3 plus the cheatsheet. Task success is primary; receptacles visited before the target is taken is the process measure; uncached prefill per episode is logged under vLLM prefix caching. The claim: on search-bound types the compiled statistic recovers at least the Gate-0 retrieval gain (~+10) over no memory at zero uncached prefill; most of that value disappears when each row is a single sample and all of it when rows are deranged; the long-context reader does not compute the statistic from the raw items; and added to the best static arm the statistic removes the ~+9 residual that k=3 retains over it on these types, while the +20..+27 procedure-bound residual is outside its scope and reported as such.
Experiments: Bank: expert pool (1,465 trajectories). Compiler (rule, no LLM): from each trajectory take the receptacle of the first successful 'take <obj> from <recep>' action; per object class (~30) emit the top-3 receptacle classes with count and percentage; ~300 tokens; identical for every game and type; placed in the instruction slot as a cached static prefix. Aggregation-depth ladder at fixed coverage (replaces the n-trajectory ladder, whose low rungs confounded coverage with depth): cheatsheet_d samples, for every object class c, min(d, n_c) trajectories containing that class and compiles the row from them; d = 1 (one sample per class, every class covered, ~150 tokens, three uniform draws), d = 4 (one draw, exploratory), d = all (the full table). Placebos: shuffled_all (receptacle lists deranged across object classes, identical tokens and format); LLM-prior (Qwen3-32B fills the same format for the same object classes and receptacle vocabulary from its own knowledge, no bank, generated once, token-matched). Whole bank: 80 expert items (~140 tokens each, ~11k tokens, cached) selected by a stated rule - stratified by task type and, within type, to cover every object class at least twice; fixed order per seed; whole-bank_80 + cheatsheet_80 adds the table compiled from exactly those 80 items (~250 tokens). Cells: cell S = the 134 search-bound games (pick-and-place, pick-two, look-at-in-light; 59 unseen + 75 seen) x 8 seeds = 1,072 paired (game, seed) cells per arm; seeds 1-2 coincide with Measurement C's cells. Confirmatory arms on cell S (12, all run fresh in one serving session so every contrast is paired within-session): k0; k3 retrieval (~430 uncached tokens); static3 (C's best static arm, 3 fixed type-conditioned exemplars, ~430 tokens cached); cheatsheet_all; shuffled_all; LLM-prior; cheatsheet_d1 x 3 draws; static3 + cheatsheet_all (~730 tokens cached); whole-bank_80; whole-bank_80 + cheatsheet_80. Exploratory arms at seeds 1-2 (268 cells, floor +-12): cheatsheet_d4; instr_all + cheatsheet_all (type-agnostic twin of the static3 combo, ~700 tokens); cheatsheet_80 alone; k3 + cheatsheet_all (additivity); and cheatsheet_all on the 140 procedure-bound games x 2 seeds (280 cells) against C's stored k0/static3/k3 cells for the scope boundary. Process measure from step logs: distinct receptacles visited before the target object is taken (episodes with no take scored at all distinct receptacles visited); steps per episode. Cost: uncached and cached prefill tokens per episode (static prefixes cached across the arm under vLLM prefix caching; retrieval prefixes uncached), tokens/s per GPU, episodes/min; accuracy-cost curves over uncached prefill. Arithmetic: 12 confirmatory arms x 1,072 = 12,864 episodes + ~1,350 exploratory = ~14.2k episodes; at the rate assumed in the original plan (548 episodes per ~30 min, ~18 episodes/min across two vLLM replicas on two A100s, workers tuned to the queue) ~13 h, plus ~1 h for the two whole-bank arms decoding against an 11k cached prefix: one overnight run, resumable JSONL under nohup. Order: (1) fresh k0 and k3 (drift check against C's stored seeds 1-2 and positive control; the bootstrap half-width on this pair fixes the floor and the margins before any confirmatory arm); (2) cheatsheet_all (headline); (3) static3, shuffled_all, LLM-prior; (4) the three d=1 draws; (5) static3 + cheatsheet_all; (6) the whole-bank pair, last among confirmatory arms so a budget overrun costs P6 and not the headline; (7) exploratory arms on idle replica time. Pre-registration file (arm list, cells, margins, decision rules, stopping rule) committed before step (2).
Baselines and Ablations: Baseline per the round rule is the best static arm: static3 (C: +12.4 over k0 overall) is re-run on cell S at 8 seeds, and every retrieval number on cell S is reported as k3 (and k7 from C's stored cells at seeds 1-2) minus the best of {static3, cheatsheet_all, static3 + cheatsheet_all}; cheatsheet_all - static3 is reported (does 300 tokens of statistic beat 430 tokens of type-conditioned exemplars on search-bound types). Type conditioning: the cheatsheet is one fixed table for all games and types; static3 is type-conditioned, so its combo has a type-agnostic twin (instr_all + cheatsheet_all). Ablations that attribute the gain: depth at fixed coverage (d = 1 vs all; d = 4 exploratory) - aggregation vs coverage; deranged table - content vs scaffold, with shuffled_all - k0 reported so 'true table helps' is separated from 'wrong table hurts'; LLM-prior table - experience vs pretraining, with the pre-registered covariate of row-level top-1 agreement between the prior and the compiled table; whole-bank_80 with and without its own table - explicit vs implicit aggregation at matched items; k3 + cheatsheet_all - additivity to retrieved procedures (exploratory). The manipulated variable is the artifact (depth, content, source) at fixed format; the search-bound/procedure-bound split is a pre-registered pooled cell, and its contrast (the statistic helps only where search is the bottleneck) is reported from the 2-seed procedure-bound arm as exploratory scope evidence, not claimed.
Falsifiable Predictions: Decision rule for every 'X - Y >= M on cell S' prediction (floor F = +-6 at 1,072 paired cells; F < M throughout): confirmed iff the paired 95% bootstrap CI excludes 0 in the predicted direction and its upper bound is >= M (the predicted size is not excluded); falsified iff the CI upper bound is < M; otherwise inconclusive and counted against the claim. With F < M a true effect of size M is falsified with probability ~2.5% and a true null is confirmed with probability ~2.5%, so 0 and M are separable. M1 = +10 = the Gate-0 retrieval gain pooled on the search-bound types (A: +15 / +18 / -4.8 weighted by game count; recomputed from stored cells and, if larger, replaced by the fresh k3 - k0 on cell S; fixed at pre-registration). M2 = +7 (two-thirds of M1: the majority of the compiled gain). P1 (headline): cheatsheet_all - k0 >= M1 on cell S. Arm: cheatsheet_all vs fresh k0. Falsified if the CI upper bound < M1 - reachable because nothing forces the reader to use a frequency table. P2 (aggregation, not coverage): cheatsheet_all - cheatsheet_d1 (mean of three draws, draws nested in the bootstrap, F ~ +-6) >= M2 on cell S. Arm: the d=1 draws vs cheatsheet_all. Falsified if the CI upper bound < M2 - reachable if one sampled placement per object class already carries the usable content, in which case the table's value is coverage, not aggregation. Between-draw SD reported; the ordering d1 < d4 < all is exploratory and unpowered (d4 at 2 seeds, F +-12). P3 (content, not scaffold): cheatsheet_all - shuffled_all >= M1 on cell S. Arm: shuffled_all. Falsified if the CI upper bound < M1 - reachable if the reader treats the table as a 'search receptacles systematically' scaffold and ignores rows. shuffled_all - k0 is reported with a pre-registered reading: if shuffled - k0 is reliably negative while cheatsheet_all - k0 is not reliably positive, P3 is not counted as support (it would show a wrong table hurts, not that the right one helps). P4 (experience, not pretraining): cheatsheet_all - LLM-prior >= M2 on cell S. Arm: LLM-prior. Falsified if the CI upper bound < M2 - reachable and plausible, since ALFWorld placements are stereotyped; that outcome means a static prompt with no experience recovers the search-bound retrieval gain and is reported as the informative negative; the pre-registered covariate (top-1 agreement between the two tables) says whether a null is redundancy (agreement high) or the reader ignoring content (agreement low, then in tension with P3). P5 (removes the residual on search-bound types): C's measured residual of k3 over the best static arm on these types is R_S ~ +9 (pick types +10..+12, look-at +4.8; exact pooled value fixed at pre-registration from C's per-game cells and re-measured fresh as k3 - static3 at 8 seeds). Prediction: k3 - (static3 + cheatsheet_all) on cell S is removed: confirmed iff the paired 95% CI upper bound < R_S and the point residual <= R_S/2; falsified otherwise (one boundary, no dead band). Arm: static3 + cheatsheet_all (730 tokens, cached, 0 uncached prefill) vs fresh k3 (430 uncached). Falsifier reachable if retrieval carries instance bindings or procedure detail on these types beyond the location statistic. P5 is run only if the fresh R_S exceeds the floor (+6); otherwise it is dropped as unresolvable at this n and the residual is reported. The residual vs k7 (1,010 tokens; C's stored cells at seeds 1-2) and the type-agnostic twin instr_all + cheatsheet_all are reported alongside. P6 (the reader is not an aggregator): (whole-bank_80 + cheatsheet_80) - whole-bank_80 >= M2 on cell S, where cheatsheet_80 is compiled from exactly the 80 items in context, so the information is present in both arms. Arm: the whole-bank pair. Falsified if the CI upper bound < M2 - reachable if the long-context reader extracts the placement statistic from the raw items itself, making the explicit table redundant. cheatsheet_80 alone vs whole-bank_80 is reported (exploratory, 2 seeds); cheatsheet_80 is no longer a rung of the depth ladder, so P2 and P6 no longer share a cell. P7 (process): distinct receptacles visited before the target object is taken, with no-take episodes scored at all distinct receptacles visited (search ran to the step limit; the restricted both-arms-take version is secondary). Predicted paired reduction >= 1.0 under cheatsheet_all vs k0 on cell S; confirmed iff the 95% CI of the reduction lies entirely above 0.5, falsified otherwise (expected half-width ~0.2-0.3 at 1,072 paired episodes, so the rule is decisive). Reachable falsifier: the reader does not act on the table. P8 (positive control and drift gate, run first): fresh k0 and k3 on cell S seeds 1-2 must each reproduce C's stored cells for the same (game, seed) within the 268-cell floor (+-12); a larger difference is serving drift and stops the run before any confirmatory arm. Fresh k3 - k0 on cell S at 8 seeds: >= +7 (0.7 x M1) - proceed as pre-registered; between 0 and +7 with CI excluding 0 - proceed with M1 fixed at +10 (the headline then asks the statistic to beat the retrieval gain outright); CI including 0 - proceed with P1..P4, P6, P7 but drop P5 (no residual to remove; a P5 test would then be entailed by P1). Shared terms are declared: P1, P3, P4 share the cheatsheet_all minuend and are one measurement with three subtrahends; P7 is scored on the same episodes as P1; they are reported as one family, not as independent confirmations.
Measurement and Noise Control: Outcome: task success on paired (game, seed) cells; net = paired difference in points. Floors: the brief's +-8 at 274 x 2 rescaled by sqrt(548/n): cell S at 134 x 8 = 1,072 cells gives +-5.7, stated as +-6; the 268-cell exploratory subsets +-12; the 280-cell procedure-bound arm +-11. The floor is verified, not assumed: the bootstrap (games resampled, seeds and compile draws nested) on the fresh k3 - k0 pair is computed before any confirmatory arm; if its 95% half-width exceeds +-6.5 (game-level heterogeneity dominating), seeds 9-10 are added to every confirmatory arm (1,340 cells, +-5.1, +25% episodes) before unblinding. Permutation test on paired differences as the secondary test. Margins: M1 = +10, M2 = +7, R_S ~ +9, all fixed at pre-registration and all above the floor; margins are measured effect sizes (A's pooled search-bound gain, C's search-bound residual), not the floor. Three-way decision rule stated once in Predictions; inconclusive outcomes are reported and counted against the claim. Multiplicity: the P1/P3/P4 family shares a minuend and is reported jointly; no claim of independence. Token accounting: cheatsheet 300 (cached) vs k3 430 (uncached); static3 + cheatsheet 730 (cached) vs k7 1,010 (uncached); cheatsheet_d1 ~150 (reported; the token difference in P2 is acknowledged and the token-matched placebo is P3); whole-bank 11k cached. Uncached prefill per episode is logged for every arm and success is plotted against it. Pre-registration file with arm list, cells, margins, decision rules, stopping rule and the M1/R_S recomputation committed before the first confirmatory arm; identical games, seeds, decoding and max steps across arms; static prefixes fixed per seed so caching is real, not modelled; all cell-S arms run in one serving session so within-session pairing holds, with C's stored cells used only for the drift gate, k7 and the procedure-bound comparison.
Preprint Collision Check: Q1 (recent, mechanism) 'compiled cheatsheet of object location priors from agent trajectories versus retrieval ALFWorld' --recent: no results (S2+HF). Q1b (recent, mechanism, shorter) 'object location prior LLM agent ALFWorld household' --recent, channel S2+HF: 'Zero-Shot Embodied Decision Making with Structured Prior Knowledge and Adaptive Calibration in ALFWorld' (WCCIS 2026, no arXiv id; LLM-free symbolic agent with hand-built object-location priors and task templates; no compilation from experience, no retrieval arm, no n sweep); 2607.00022 PerSim (household object search with population-frequency priors, robotics); 2605.05413 (procedural context moved to weights); 2602.06459 UcON (habit retrieval for object navigation). None compares a compiled location statistic with retrieved trajectories at matched tokens in an LLM agent. home: Q2 'object receptacle co-occurrence prior household object search semantic prior' (no agent/memory/retrieval/experience/benchmark words), channel S2+HF: 2607.00022, 2606.15476 FARM, 2603.21887 IGV-RRT, 2603.05642 SymSearch (LLM relational knowledge distilled offline into lightweight models for object search) - the mechanism is established in robotics; none is an in-context artifact compared with per-query retrieval. Q3 (closest named method) 'Dynamic Cheatsheet test-time learning adaptive memory', channel S2+HF: 2504.07952 Dynamic Cheatsheet (persistent evolving insight memory; no retrieval-vs-compiled comparison, no experience-size sweep), 2606.05684 AdaMEM, 2511.20857 Evo-Memory. Verdict: no pre-emption; the nearest overlap is the WCCIS 2026 symbolic-agent paper, which motivates rather than tests the claim.
Risk Factors and Limitations: The prior may be commonsense the model already holds (P4 falsifier); reported as an informative negative for the area, with the agreement covariate saying which kind. ALFWorld placements are sampled from generic plausibility, so the compiled statistic is scene-agnostic; environments with scene-specific placements would need a scene key (a different study). Only Qwen3-32B; the reader's use of a frequency table may differ by backbone. The search-bound cell is 134 games, so the 8-seed floor rests on the brief's sqrt rescaling; if game-level heterogeneity dominates, the adaptive seed rule adds 25% episodes and the total grows to ~17 h. The d=1 rungs have fewer tokens than the full table (~150 vs ~300); P2 therefore confounds depth with the number of listed alternatives, which is the content aggregation produces; the token-matched placebo (P3) and the same-format prior (P4) bound that confound. The search-bound/procedure-bound split is a named property, not a manipulated one; the claim's dependence on it is reported from the 2-seed procedure-bound arm as exploratory scope evidence, and the manipulated variable is the artifact. Measurement C's stored cells enter only through the drift gate, k7 and the procedure-bound comparison; if the drift gate fails the study stops rather than mixing sessions. The rule compiler assumes a 'take X from Y' step in every expert trajectory (true by construction; checked). Whole-bank arms decode against an 11k prefix and are the slowest; they are scheduled last among confirmatory arms so a budget overrun costs P6, not the headline. P1, P3 and P4 share a measured minuend and are one family; a single bad cheatsheet_all cell moves all three.
Addresses gap: G1 (the source of any compilation gain - distillation vs weighting vs extra context - is unresolved): the depth ladder at fixed coverage, the deranged table and the no-experience table attribute the gain to aggregation of experience at fixed format; also G3 (whole-bank arm with and without its own compiled statistic at matched items) and G5 (gain vs aggregation depth; cost per episode under caching, accuracy-cost curves over uncached prefill).
Not a restatement of: Prior-result bullet 'Measurement A: gain carried by clean/heat/cool procedures, pick-and-place +15, pick-two +18, look-at -4.8; unseen ~ seen, so the retrieved value is the type's procedure': this idea claims a second kind of value on the search-bound types, a cross-episode statistic that k retrieved trajectories cannot contain, and predicts it recovers retrieval's gain there and removes the residual C leaves over the best static arm on those types. Measurement C bullet 'static3 - k0 = +12.4; k3 - static3 = +17.2': C's static arms are exemplars and procedures; this idea adds a static artifact of a different kind, names the manipulation (adding the statistic) that removes the search-bound part of the +17.2, and states that the procedure-bound part is outside its reach. Digest card arxiv:2511.07800 (strategy graph distilled from trajectories; source of gain unclear): this idea fixes the output format and varies aggregation depth at fixed coverage, deranges the content and removes the experience, so the gain is attributed to aggregation rather than to extra context or distillation.
Changes made: P1 (was unresolvable): floor shrunk below the margin - the search-bound cell is run at 8 seeds (134 games, 1,072 cells, floor +-6) against a margin of +10 (A's measured Gate-0 gain pooled on these types, not +12), with a three-way decision rule under which 0 and +10 are separable (a true +10 is falsified ~2.5% of the time); adaptive seed rule if the bootstrap half-width exceeds +-6.5. P2 (was near_entailed): the n-trajectory ladder (6/20/80/1465), whose low rung confounded coverage with depth, replaced by a depth ladder at fixed coverage (every object class compiled from d = 1, 4, all sampled trajectories); the confirmatory contrast is d = 1 (three draws) vs the full table with margin +7 > floor; the monotone ordering declared exploratory and unpowered. P3: shuffled_all - k0 added with a pre-registered reading that separates 'true table helps' from 'wrong table hurts'. P4: row-level top-1 agreement between the prior and compiled tables pre-registered as a covariate. P5: restated against C's measured residual on the search-bound types (R_S ~ +9, re-measured fresh) instead of an assumed null, as the brief requires; a single decision boundary (CI upper < R_S and point <= R_S/2) closes the dead band; the combo uses C's best static arm (static3) with the type-agnostic twin run as a control; the 'matches k=3 on all types' clause dropped because C's instr_all is -20.1 under k3 and a location statistic cannot carry the +20..+27 procedure residual - the procedure-bound cell is now the stated scope boundary, tested at 2 seeds. P6: reduced to the explicit-vs-implicit aggregation contrast at matched items with cheatsheet_80 compiled from exactly the 80 in-context items and no longer a ladder rung, so P2 and P6 no longer share a cell; the 80-item selection rule is stated. P7: estimand fixed (no-take episodes scored at all receptacles visited; restricted version secondary) and one decision rule (CI above 0.5). P8: explicit consequence in every band (drift stops the run; a small fresh gain keeps M1 = +10; a null fresh gain drops P5 as entailed). Budget: 12 confirmatory arms x 1,072 + ~1,350 exploratory ~ 14.2k episodes ~ 14 h on two A100s, whole-bank arms last so an overrun costs P6 not the headline; the k3 + cheatsheet additivity arm and the d = 4 rung demoted to 2-seed exploratory. Kept sharp: the headline still asks a 300-token cached table to match retrieval's gain on search-bound types at zero uncached prefill; it still predicts that a single-sample table loses most of the gain, a deranged one all of it, and that the raw bank in context does not reproduce it; and instead of a hedged 'closes the gap' it now names the manipulation that removes C's measured search-bound residual over the best static arm. Margins were moved to measured effect sizes, not lowered to the floor.

Name: retrieval_timing_is_budgeting
Title: When to Retrieve Is Only a Budget Question: A Harm-Mass Bound on the Value of Retrieval Timing for Experience Memory, Tested at Two Distractor Levels, With Failure-Keyed Retrieval at Stall Against Planted Recoveries, Coverage-Matched Self Detours and a Compiled Rulebook
Short Hypothesis: With retrieved content, cached prefix and message format held fixed, the value of any retrieval-timing policy (start, fixed schedule, on stall, learned) over always-retrieve is bounded above by the harm mass: the fraction of episodes on which retrieval breaks an episode the static prompt solves, beyond test-retest flips. On ALFWorld we measure the harm mass as a paired-table estimand at two distractor levels of one expert bank and predict it is inside the +/-8 floor at the natural bank and above it with mislabelled twins. Stall-triggered retrieval then sits within the floor of always-retrieve at the natural bank in both directions, overall and on the rows where the trigger fires, and re-delivering the already-read block at the stall adds nothing; at the twin bank it gains over a separately run always-retrieve replicate by at least 8 net but never more than the harm mass plus the floor, and solves no episodes beyond test-retest that neither the static prompt nor the start read solves, so timing re-trades uncached tokens for the same success and cannot buy more. A failure-keyed query at stall beats a content-free key only when the bank holds matching recoveries: at matched coverage the agent's own curated detours do as well as planted recoveries, the natural self pool does not, and a compiled recovery rulebook in the cached prefix matches planted retrieval at zero uncached cost.
Related Work: arXiv:2607.24010 (When Should Active RAG Retrieve?) recasts active retrieval as marginal correctness over the no-retrieval answer under a budget, but on QA with document retrieval, without a harm-mass estimand on paired seeds, a stall trigger or caching costs. ProactAgent (arXiv:2604.20572, 'Ask Only When Needed') retrieves proactively from memory and skills for lifelong agents without an always-retrieve-at-matched-content arm or an upper bound on the decision. FLARE (arXiv:2305.06983) and Adaptive-RAG (arXiv:2403.14403) trigger retrieval by uncertainty or complexity in QA. Reflexion (arXiv:2303.11366) conditions on failure across trials, not within-episode stalls, and has no static control. Digest: arXiv:2607.07380 (hidden-state uncertainty decides when to retrieve; no always/never baselines), s2:93def179dbebdaf187c0bce1f494a2bbd39ddc19 (RL proxy decides when/how; cost unaccounted), arXiv:2510.16724 (survey; no common protocol), arXiv:2607.20972 (cue-triggered deterministic injection beats voluntary reads; no harm bound or compiled control), arXiv:2505.00234 (self-generated examples for sequential decision tasks, the on-policy bank). Archived ideas do not address timing; compile_dont_retrieve concerns the goal-conditioned read at episode start.
Abstract: Adaptive retrieval papers ask when to retrieve but do not report what a perfect answer to that question would be worth. For experience memory under prompt caching the accounting is simple: with the retrieved content, the cached prefix and the message format held fixed, a timing policy can add success over always-retrieve only on episodes where retrieval breaks an episode the static prompt would have solved. We call that fraction the harm mass and measure it as a pre-registered paired-table estimand on ALFWorld (Qwen3-32B, 274 games x 2 seeds, static3 cached prefix from Measurement C, one k=3 goal-keyed block appended at step 0 or later): P(static succeeds and retrieval fails) minus the same discordance between two static runs, at two distractor levels of one expert bank (natural, and a 1:1 mislabelled-twin bank in which goal-keyed retrieval returns a wrong-type trajectory in about half the slots). Predictions: the harm mass is inside the +/-8 floor at the natural bank and above it with twins; stall-triggered retrieval (two consecutive 'Nothing happens' or a repeated action) is within the floor of always-retrieve at the natural bank in both directions, overall and on the rows where the trigger fires, and re-delivering the already-read block at the stall adds nothing; at the twin bank it gains over a separately run always-retrieve replicate by at least 8 net and by no more than the harm mass plus the floor, with the bound estimated from the other replicate so bound and gain cannot co-move, and the late-read-only mass (episodes the stall arm solves that neither the static prompt nor the start read solves, beyond test-retest) stays inside the floor; a fixed step-10 schedule does the same as the trigger. We then ask whether the query at stall matters, separating key from content in a k=1 2x2 (failure key vs random key; planted-recovery bank vs expert pool) and manipulating recovery coverage in the agent's own detour pool (natural coverage measured by a validated tagger; curated recovery windows at coverage near 1). Predictions: the failure key beats a random key only with planted recoveries; curated self detours match planted recoveries at matched coverage while the natural pool falls short; and a ~200-token recovery rulebook in the cached prefix matches planted retrieval at zero uncached cost. The output is an accuracy-cost frontier on which the timing decision moves along the frontier rather than above it, with the bound tested as an inequality at a level where it binds, the one channel that could breach it measured directly, and a test of whether any query is more than decorative at stall time.
Experiments: Setting as in Measurement A/C: ALFWorld 274 games x 2 seeds, identical game seeds across arms, Qwen3-32B on two vLLM replicas with prefix caching. Shared prefix: static3 (3 fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars, ~430 tokens, cached), Measurement C's best static arm; every arm sits on it. Retrieval block: k=3 goal-keyed items (~430 tokens) appended as one environment-style message with identical text and format at step 0 (always), step 10 (schedule), the stall (stall arms) or both (double-read), so content, prefix and format are fixed and only the delivery step varies. Banks: natural expert bank; distractor bank = expert bank plus one mislabelled twin per item (its goal sentence attached to the trajectory of a different-type expert item sharing the target object), so goal-keyed retrieval ties twins with originals and returns a wrong-type trajectory in about half the k=3 slots; planted-recovery bank (five ALFWorld failure modes: closed receptacle, wrong receptacle, object already held, wrong object instance, missing 'go to'; one ~40-token recovery item each, keyed by failure text; coverage 1.0 by construction); self pool = 1,892 self-generated successes with detours, indexed by failed-action windows (natural level), and its curated subset of windows the tagger marks as a failure mode followed by a recovery within three steps (curated level); coverage and tagger validation under Baselines. Stall trigger: first occurrence of two consecutive 'Nothing happens' or a repeated (observation, action) pair; firing is fixed by the static3 trajectory before any read, so a stall arm's firing rows are outcome-blind. Queries at stall: goal sentence (k=3, matching always); failure key = last three actions and observations (k=1); random key = uniform draw from the pool (k=1); k=1 wherever the one-item-per-mode planted bank is a comparator. Estimands Delta_harm(L) and Lambda(L) are defined under P1 and P6 (static3_A = the Measurement C cell, static3_B = a fresh re-run); the cross-fitted oracle is descriptive only, no cell. Cells (548 episodes each; ~30 min on one replica, two cells concurrently): (1) static3_B; (2) always-natural; (3) always-distractor_A; (3b) always-distractor_B, a second separately sampled run on the same game seeds (as static3_B is to static3_A), the comparator for P6's gain so that bound (from cell 3) and gain share no run; (4) stall goal-key k=3, natural; (5) stall goal-key k=3, distractor; (6) step-10 schedule, natural; (6b) double-read natural: the block at step 0 and the identical block again at the stall (the goal-keyed analogue of cell 13); (7) stall failure-key k=1, expert pool; (8) stall failure-key k=1, planted; (9) stall random-key k=1, planted; (10) stall failure-key k=1, self natural; (11) stall failure-key k=1, self curated; (12) static3 + recovery rulebook (the five planted items concatenated, ~200 tokens, cached; the planted bank's whole-bank arm); (13) rulebook + stall failure-key k=1 planted. Name: whole_bank_confusability_ladder
Title: Confusable, Not Long: The Whole-Bank-in-Context Route Loses to Top-k Retrieval Only as Near-Miss Trajectories Accumulate
Short Hypothesis: On a six-procedure trajectory bank read by Qwen3-32B, the whole bank as a cached static prefix matches goal-sentence top-3 retrieval on task success up to the 16k context no matter how many redundant or off-domain items are added, and falls behind only as the count of near-miss items (same object and receptacle words, different procedure) grows. Retrieval is hurt by near-miss items too, but its exposure is capped at k items whose cross-type share equals the bank's share, so at fixed share it is flat in count. At matched length, composition therefore costs the whole-bank route more than retrieval; this route x composition interaction replicates on an independent bank draw and is larger for the weaker reader (Qwen3-8B) on the same size grid, so the bank size at which the routes cross is set by composition and reader, not prompt length.
Related Work: Enrich-Retrieve-Rank (arxiv:2608.22695) shows in-context routing over a capability registry collapsing as the registry grows while retrieve-then-rank degrades gracefully, but scores Match@1 with one router model and grows the number of distinct options, not the number of confusable copies. Bertsch et al. (arxiv:2405.00200) and arxiv:2412.16926 find that long-context ICL gains come from attention to the similar examples and that selection matters less as shots grow, on classification tasks; MANYICLBENCH (arxiv:2411.07130) separates similar-sample from all-sample learning; arxiv:2510.16809 finds a few well-chosen examples beating many on code translation. arxiv:2607.26497 measures a corpus-size crossover between agentic search and BM25 on documents with one reader; arxiv:2603.04814 measures Mem0 against long context on conversational QA with one model; arxiv:2411.05000 shows effective context shorter than advertised on synthetic threads. The compliance trap (arxiv:2607.10608) shows agents adopting conflicting retrieved memory; SkillEvolBench (arxiv:2605.24117) reports clutter from larger libraries under an unspecified selection. None of these grows a trajectory bank while holding the procedure count fixed and separating redundant count, off-domain length and confusable count, scores task success, and checks whether the crossover moves with the reader.
Abstract: Agent-memory papers assume a bank of trajectories must be queried because the whole bank will not fit or will not be read well, and the long-context literature reports crossovers between retrieval and in-context reading measured on documents with one reader. We ask what property of a trajectory bank actually makes the whole-bank-in-context route fall behind top-k retrieval on task success. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B we grow a six-item seed bank (one expert exemplar per task type) to 12-80 items in three ways that hold the six procedures fixed: redundant growth (same-type items whose object-receptacle combos collide with no other type), off-domain filler (token-matched trajectories from another text game), and near-miss growth (every added item has a twin of another type with the same object and receptacle, so half the bank is confusable). Each bank is read whole as a cached static prefix or through goal-sentence top-3 retrieval, on the same 274 games and two seeds, with the Measurement C static arms as the baseline, a type-conditioned retrieval arm and logged top-3 composition to show that retrieved twins are actually adopted rather than merely present, a fixed uniformly random 80-item subset as the selection control, and an independent second bank draw on which the route x composition interaction is confirmed. We predict the whole-bank route is flat under redundant and filler growth and declines with the near-miss count, while retrieval is hurt by twins but flat in count at fixed share, so at matched length composition costs the whole-bank route more than retrieval, and more so for Qwen3-8B on the same size grid. Prefill tokens and GPU-seconds under prefix caching are logged for accuracy-cost curves.
Experiments:
- Bank construction from the expert pool (1,465 items). Seed S6 = one expert exemplar per task type, fixed. Growth rules that keep six procedures: R (redundant, near-miss share 0; sizes 12/48/80): add same-type items whose (object, receptacle) combo appears in no item of another type in the bank. N (near-miss, share 0.5; sizes 12/24/48/80): add items in cross-type twin pairs (same object and receptacle, different procedure; twins chosen so their first actions coincide), so at every size half the items have a twin in the bank; combos sampled from the pool's combo distribution. F (filler, size 80): S6 plus token-matched trajectories from public TextWorld cooking games in the same format with no ALFWorld nouns. U: one uniformly random fixed 80-subset of the pool (natural near-miss share measured and reported) as the G17 fixed-random-selection control. Replicate draw: a second N'-80 and R'-80 built by the same rules from disjoint items and disjoint twin combos with a fresh type-interleaved order. Per bank and size the coverage fraction (share of the 274 test goals whose combo has a twin pair in the bank) is logged. Item order type-interleaved, fixed per arm.
- Routes. WB: whole bank as a type-agnostic static prefix (vLLM prefix caching on, cache hit ratio logged). RET: goal-sentence top-3 from the same bank per episode (uncached), same retriever as Measurement A; per episode the top-3 type composition is logged (cross-type-in-top-3 rate = any item of another type in the top-3; strict twin rate = an item with the goal's object and receptacle and another type). RET-T: top-3 restricted to items of the goal's template type (type-conditioned by construction, reported under the type-conditioning rule), on N-48 only. RET-rand: three random items from the same bank, fixed per game, on N-48 only. All arms run the same 274 games x 2 seeds.
- Arms at Qwen3-32B (23): WB S6; WB R-12/48/80; WB N-12/24/48/80; RET R-12/48/80; RET N-12/24/48/80; RET-T N-48; RET-rand N-48; WB F-80; WB U-80; replicate WB N'-80, WB R'-80, RET N'-80, RET R'-80. The static baselines k0, static3, instr_all, blind1 and RET k=3 on the full pool are Measurement A/C cells on disk, paired on the same games and seeds.
- Reader manipulation (G16) at Qwen3-8B (12 arms): WB and RET on N-12/24/48/80 (the same grid as 32B), WB and RET on R-80, k0 and static3. Precondition run first: 8B static3 minus k0 must exceed +8 net; if it does not, Qwen3-14B replaces 8B as the weaker reader with the same 12 arms, decided before any ladder cell of the weaker reader is run; the reader arm is never reported as uninformative.
- Error signature: in failed episodes, the fraction whose executed action sequence follows a twin procedure (skipped or inserted clean/heat/cool step), read from the action log per route, size and reader; WB success is also split by covered vs uncovered goals per size.
- Cost: GPU-seconds per episode at fixed concurrency (16 workers per replica), prefill tokens per episode, cache hit ratio; accuracy-cost curves per route and size; the cost crossover is reported separately from the accuracy contrasts.
- Budget arithmetic: 23 arms x 548 episodes = 12,604 episodes at 32B; the 8 WB arms at 48/80 items run 2-3x slower per episode (about 2.5 GPU-h each) and the other 15 about 1 GPU-h each, about 35 GPU-h, i.e. about 17.5 h wall on the two A100s with one vLLM replica per GPU and slow WB arms interleaved with RET arms on each replica; 12 arms x 548 = 6,576 episodes at 8B at roughly a third of the per-episode cost, about 6 GPU-h, 3 h wall. Total about 20 h.
- Order: pre-registration (the positive control is already met on Measurement C: the wrong-type placebo blind1 sits 15.4 net below static3); R and N ladders at 32B; RET-T, RET-rand, F, U; replicate draw; then the weaker reader.
Baselines and Ablations:
- Static baselines (Measurement C, on disk, same games and seeds): k0; static3 (best static arm, +12.4 over k0); instr_all (type-agnostic six-procedure prompt); blind1 (wrong-type fixed exemplar: length placebo and near-miss positive control, 15.4 net below static3 and 3 below k0). Every WB and RET cell is reported minus static3 and minus instr_all at its stated tokens; WB at S6 is itself the smallest whole-bank static arm.
- RET k=3 over the natural pool (Measurement A, +17.2 over static3) and RET-rand on N-48 (three random items from the same bank, fixed per game) at the same token budget, to separate the retriever from the exemplar budget.
- RET-T on N-48: type-conditioned retrieval over the same near-miss bank; isolates twin retrieval from item identity (N items are selected for having twins, so N and R banks differ in which expert items they contain).
- WB F-80 isolates prompt length from content; WB U-80 is the matched-budget random-selection control at the whole-context budget and supplies a third, natural near-miss share.
- Replicate bank draw (N'-80, R'-80, both routes) gives the confirmatory interaction cells and absorbs item-identity and order variation between draws.
- Reader ablation: the weaker reader on the full N ladder and at R-80, plus its own k0 and static3.
Falsifiable Predictions:
All contrasts are paired net differences over 274 x 2 with one threshold, 9 net: a decline is confirmed at or below -9 and falsified above it; flatness is confirmed inside +/-9 and falsified at or beyond it.
- P1 (length and redundancy do not hurt the whole-bank route): WB(R-80) - WB(S6) and WB(F-80) - WB(S6) are both within +/-9. Falsified if either is at or below -9 (plain long-context degradation of an 80-item prefix); arms: WB R-80 and WB F-80 against WB S6.
- P2 (confusable count hurts the whole-bank route): at matched length WB(N-80) - WB(R-80) is at or below -9, WB declines monotonically over N-12/24/48/80, and the twin-procedure fraction among WB failures rises by at least 10 points from N-12 to N-80. Falsified if WB(N-80) - WB(R-80) is above -9, or if the decline is not accompanied by the error-signature rise (a generic length or attention failure). Reachable: blind1 costs only 3 net against k0 on Measurement C, so a 32B reader that disambiguates by the goal sentence leaves WB(N-80) flat; arms: WB N-80, WB R-80, WB N-12.
- P3 (retrieved twins are exposed and adopted; retrieval exposure is share-bound, not count-bound): (a) on N-48 the logged cross-type-in-top-3 rate is at least 0.4 (and at most 0.15 on R-48), RET(N-48) - RET(R-48) is at or below -9, and RET-T(N-48) - RET(R-48) is within +/-9. Falsified if the retriever does not expose twins (rate below 0.4 on N-48), if the reader ignores exposed twins (rate reached yet RET(N-48) - RET(R-48) above -9, reachable because a wrong-type item beside a right-type one may be disambiguated as blind1 nearly is against k0), or if RET-T(N-48) stays at or below -9 against RET(R-48) (the N-bank penalty is item identity, not twins). (b) at fixed share RET(N-80) - RET(N-12) is within +/-9, with the cross-type-in-top-3 rate reported per size. Falsified if RET(N-80) - RET(N-12) is at or below -9 (retrieval declines with count, for instance because twin coverage of test goals grows with the number of pairs). Name: recall_success_dissociation
Title: Recall Ranks Retrievers, Success Does Not: A Two-Environment Audit of Experience Retrieval Against the Static Prompt with Manipulated Duplicate Availability
Short Hypothesis: Retriever recall (fraction of top-k items sharing the test task's type or binding) and the task-success residual over the best static prompt built from the same bank dissociate, and the dissociation is set by whether the retrieved binding is recoverable inside the episode. On ALFWorld the measured +17.2 net of BM25 k=3 over static3 is an exemplar-source effect, not a recall effect: a static prompt of three fixed self-generated bank exemplars of the goal's type sits within the ±8 floor of BM25, and above type recall the map is flat through same-scene recall (oracle same-scene at coverage 0/0.5/1) and exact same-game duplicates, because layout and object location are recoverable by looking. On WebShop, where the binding (which product satisfies the attribute set) is expensive to recover by search, the residual over the best static arm appears only when a same-product trajectory is in the bank, rises with the fraction of instructions for which one is retrieved (coverage 0/0.5/1), and the natural BM25 retriever's gain equals its measured product recall times the oracle gain. Recall above the type threshold is therefore uninformative unless the bank carries non-recoverable bindings, and retriever evaluation must report the success residual over a static arm built from the same bank at two or more duplicate-availability levels.
Related Work: 2604.04949 trains retrievers from agent trajectories and reports evidence recall and task success together with no random or fixed control, so recall and success are never dissociated. 2512.20854 correlates retrieval metrics with LLM-judged answer quality in RAG QA and 2508.05909 tries to isolate the retriever's contribution to a reader; both are single-turn QA with no static arm. 2603.02473 finds retrieval dominates write strategy on LoCoMo (QA, no full-history or fixed arm). SWE-ContextBench (2602.08316) shows correctly selected related-task experience helps and mis-selected experience harms on dependency-linked tasks, without a random or static control; 2607.10608 shows wrong retrieved memory is adopted at the first decision point. Traj-Bootstrap (2505.00234) and ExpeL/Reflexion report ALFWorld and WebShop memory gains over no memory only. Measurement A on this node observed unseen approximately equal to seen with one retriever and no static arm. Measurement C on this node (274 x 2) measured k3 minus static3 = +17.2 net over three fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars, with no static arm built from the bank itself and no manipulation of what the retrieved items share with the test game. Archived decorative_retriever (5.75) observed retrieval-set overlap without manipulating it.
Abstract: Retrievers for agent memory are ranked by recall of relevant items; whether that ranking survives when the outcome is task success over the best static prompt built from the same experience is unknown, and it should depend on whether the retrieved item carries something the agent cannot recover inside the episode. On ALFWorld, BM25 retrieval at k=3 beats three fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars by a measured +17.2 net; we claim this residual is an exemplar-source effect, not a recall effect. We manipulate two things on two environments with Qwen3-32B: retriever recall (random-type, same-type-random, goal-BM25, oracle same-binding, exact duplicate, all at k=3) and the bank's duplicate availability (oracle same-binding items retained for a nested 0/50/100% of test tasks: scene on ALFWorld, goal product on WebShop). Every arm is paired on (task, seed) with static arms built from the same bank (fixed bank exemplars per type and type-agnostic, compiled procedure, whole bank in a 16k context), and the comparator is selected on separate seeds or a held-out set so no residual is computed on the cells that chose its baseline. Predictions: on ALFWorld a static prompt of three fixed bank exemplars of the goal's type sits within the ±8 floor of BM25, and the residual is flat from type recall through same-scene coverage (slope within ±8 per unit coverage) and exact same-game duplicates; on WebShop, on the subset of test instructions with a same-product success in the bank, the residual rises with coverage (slope at least +16 per unit) and the natural BM25 gain equals its measured product recall times the oracle gain, while with duplicates removed no retriever clears the floor over the static arm. A positive control (BM25 over k=0 on WebShop) gates the residual-over-static claims; the coverage contrasts are comparator-free. The audit yields a rule for evaluating experience retrievers: report success residual over a static arm built from the same bank at two duplicate-availability levels, and treat recall above the type threshold as uninformative unless the bank carries bindings the episode cannot recover.
Experiments: E0 ALFWorld bank and pools (about 2,400 episodes, about 2 h): A's bank and C's arm definitions are reused; the bank is supplemented by k=0 runs (2 seeds) on train games in the valid_seen scenes so that every valid_seen game has at least one (typically three) same-type same-scene success (games without one are reported and excluded from the coverage arms; expected under 5%); the exact-duplicate pool is each valid_seen game's own k=0 or static3 success from C's seeds, defining the subset G (expected at least 80 games; one extra non-evaluation static3 seed, 140 episodes, is run if smaller). All new ALFWorld runs are on valid_seen (140 games) with fresh seeds disjoint from C's: two selection seeds (3-4) and four evaluation seeds (5-8). E1 ALFWorld static arms, 140 x 6 = 840 cells each: k0; static3 (C's three fixed type-conditioned expert exemplars, about 430 tokens); static3-bank (three fixed bank successes per type, chosen once as BM25 medoids of the type, token-matched to static3); instr_all (type-agnostic six-procedure prompt); whole-bank (bank in context up to 16k, same-type items first, shortest-first within type, rule pre-registered). Comparator rule: the static arm with the highest mean success on seeds 3-4 (280 cells; ties within 4 net resolved toward static3); all residuals are computed on seeds 5-8 only (560 cells). 4,200 episodes. E2 ALFWorld retrieval ladder at k=3, seeds 5-8, 560 cells each: random-type (uniform over the bank; type recall about 1/6); same-type-random (uniform over same-type items; type recall 1, object-class and scene recall at base rate); BM25 on goal text over the natural bank (scene recall b_alf measured); oracle-scene at coverage c in {0, 0.5, 1}: for a pre-registered nested fraction c of games the same-type same-scene items are ranked first (by BM25 score among themselves), remaining slots filled by BM25 over other scenes; c=0 is BM25 with every same-scene item excluded, so per-cell scene recall equals c by construction; oracle-game on G: the game's own success at rank 1 plus two BM25 items. 7 x 560 = 3,920 episodes. ALFWorld total about 10,500 episodes, about 10 h on one vLLM replica at about 1,100 episodes/h. E3 WebShop setup and bank (one day of setup; about 4,800 episodes, about 3.7 h): Qwen3-32B ReAct agent on the WebShop text environment; T = the 500 standard test instructions; L = train instructions whose goal product equals a test goal product (count reported), run at k=0 with two seeds, plus random train instructions at one seed up to 3,000 instructions; successes (score = 1) form the bank; S = test instructions with at least one same-product bank success, pre-registered minimum 150 and cap 250 (fallback 1: the public human demonstrations are added to the bank; fallback 2: the exact-instruction rung X becomes the primary WebShop duplicate level and is labelled as a weaker binding); a held-out set of 300 train instructions not in the bank is reserved for comparator selection; the floor replicate (k0 on T with two non-evaluation seeds, 1,000 episodes) also supplies the exact-instruction pool and the subset X of test instructions with at least one own success. About 7,200-9,000 episodes. WebShop total about 20,000-23,000 episodes, 15-18 h on one replica at about 1,300 episodes/h. E6 gate: BM25 k=3 (natural bank) minus k0 on T must clear the WebShop floor before any residual-over-static claim on WebShop; the comparator-free coverage contrasts are tested regardless. Two environments are two points; the rule is a prediction to test on a third.

Name: relocated_bindings_demand
Title: Relocate the Mug: Binding Demand and Binding Supply, Not Bank Content, Decide Whether Experience Retrieval Beats a Compiled Procedure
Short Hypothesis: On template environments the retrieval gain is procedure-bound because nothing instance-specific is both required for success and unguessable from priors; if the environment is edited so that the target object sits off its canonical receptacle (relocated PDDL initial state) and search is expensive (tight step budget), a scene-keyed retrieval residual over the best static prompt appears, but only when the bank contains a same-scene item carrying the new location, and a cached location table with one row per (scene, object class) recovers the same residual at zero uncached tokens.
Related Work: Measurement A on this node (k=3 retrieval +27/+32 net, unseen approximately equal to seen) and Measurement C (five static arms) are the starting position. RAP (arXiv:2402.03610) retrieves past experiences by current situation on ALFWorld/WebShop but never compares against a fixed exemplar set or a compiled prompt at matched tokens. State-grounded dynamic retrieval for web agents (arXiv:2606.04391) keys retrieval on page state but does not manipulate whether state matters. VTM-Nav (arXiv:2607.14514) reuses object locations across episodes in fixed scenes with no static control. SWE-ContextBench (arXiv:2602.08316) shows correctly selected related-task experience helps, with relatedness observed rather than manipulated. SGR-Bench (arXiv:2605.22219) attributes failures to site-specific state but never tests supplying stored procedures. The compliance trap (arXiv:2607.10608) shows agents adopt wrong retrieved memory; we use its stale-binding case as an exploratory arm. Archived ideas decorative_retriever (overlap observed, not manipulated) and abstraction_discards_bindings_and_repairs (memory representation manipulated, environment demand held fixed) are the nearest prior ideas.
Abstract: Experience-memory papers report retrieval gains over no memory, but on template benchmarks such as ALFWorld the goal sentence reveals the procedure and a static prompt built once from the same experience captures most of the gain (Measurement A: unseen approximately equal to seen). We ask which environment property makes a query necessary and manipulate it directly rather than naming it. Binding demand is manipulated at two levels by editing the PDDL initial state of every evaluation game so that the target object is moved to a receptacle where its class never appears in training (canonical vs relocated), crossed with the step budget (50 vs 25); the relocation rule is deterministic per (scene, object class) so that sibling games in the same scene share the binding. Binding supply is manipulated by the bank: scene-matched fresh siblings (regenerated by the ALFWorld PDDL expert under relocation), scene-disjoint items only (valid_seen purged of same-scene items; valid_unseen replicates this by construction), and, exploratorily, stale same-scene items from the canonical games. Arms in every cell: k=0, goal-query retrieval k=3 (Measurement A), scene-query retrieval k=3 (query = goal plus initial room observation), type-conditioned fixed exemplars, type-agnostic all-six-procedures prompt, a random-type length placebo, a whole-bank arm (the type's 80 nearest items including the sibling), and a compiled location table (all six procedures plus one row per (scene, class) with the relocated receptacle, at most 274 rows, about 3k cached tokens). Every retrieval claim is reported as retrieval minus the best static arm on the same (game, seed), with uncached prefill tokens per episode logged. The design predicts a zero residual without demand or without supply, a residual of at least half the Gate-0 gain with both, and its recovery by the table without any query; each of these can fail in a named cell.
Experiments: 1. Construction: for each of the 274 eval games (valid_seen + valid_unseen) compute the canonical receptacle set of the target class from train (receptacles holding the class in >=5% of train games); relocate the object (both objects for pick-two) to a type-compatible, non-goal receptacle in the same scene outside that set, deterministic per (scene, class); edit the PDDL problem init; run the ALFWorld PDDL expert to verify solvability and to produce the fresh expert trajectory; drop and count games the planner cannot solve. Apply the same rule to all train games in the eval scenes to obtain the sibling supply (fresh relocated expert items). 2. Manipulation check (first, positive control): k=0 at canonical x {50, 25} and relocated x {50, 25}, 274 x 2 seeds each. Pre-registered escalation: if relocated x 25 does not drop k=0 success by >= 8 net vs canonical x 25, run one further level (budget 15 or +10 distractor objects in closed receptacles); if still no drop, stop and report the demand lever as inert. 3. Confirmatory cells (each arm 274 x 2 seeds, ~30 min): relocated x tight x fresh-sibling supply: goal-query k=3, scene-query k=3, type-agnostic static, compiled table, type-conditioned 3 exemplars, placebo; canonical x tight: goal-query, scene-query, type-agnostic; relocated x loose x fresh supply: scene-query, type-agnostic; relocated x tight x scene-disjoint supply: scene-query. 4. Exploratory: relocated x tight x stale-sibling supply (scene-query) for the compliance-trap direction; whole-bank arm at relocated x tight x fresh supply; per-type breakdown (clean/heat/cool vs pick-and-place vs pick-two vs look-at). 5. Cost: prefill tokens per episode split into cached (static prefix, vLLM prefix cache hits) and uncached (retrieved items), plus retriever wall-clock; accuracy-cost curve per cell. Total ~8,500 episodes, ~7-8 h at 20 episodes/min on two A100s (one vLLM replica per GPU).
Baselines and Ablations: Baselines (static, cached): type-agnostic all-six-procedures prompt (~400 tokens); type-conditioned 3 fixed expert exemplars (~430 tokens, matched to k=3); compiled location table (procedures + <=274 rows); random-type 3-exemplar length placebo; whole-bank 80-item arm (~11k tokens) as the no-query information-complete arm. Retrieval arms: goal-query k=3 (Measurement A retriever, unchanged) and scene-query k=3 (same embedding model, index text = goal + first observation). Ablations: supply (fresh sibling / scene-disjoint / stale sibling); demand (canonical/relocated x 50/25 steps); k=1 and k=7 for the scene-query arm at the positive cell; table with rows shuffled vs sorted by scene (lost-in-the-middle check); table restricted to the 20 rows of the current scene's classes (a cheaper compiled variant); second seed pair to check seed stability of the positive cell.
Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (positive control) k=0 success at relocated x 25 steps is >= 8 net below canonical x 25 steps. Falsified if the drop is < 8 net; produced by the two k=0 cells. If falsified after the pre-registered escalation the demand lever is reported inert and the confirmatory cells are not run. P2 (no residual without demand) In canonical x 25 and in relocated x 50, scene-query retrieval minus type-agnostic static is <= +8 net. Falsified by a residual >= +8 in either cell (produced by the canonical x tight x scene-query cell or the relocated x loose x scene-query cell), meaning the residual is not gated by demand. P3 (residual with demand and supply) In relocated x 25 x fresh-sibling supply, scene-query retrieval minus type-agnostic static is >= +14 net (half the Gate-0 gain of 27). Falsified by < +8 net in that cell, meaning the reader cannot apply a location from a retrieved trajectory even when required (application failure, G7). P4 (binding-bound, not content-bound) In relocated x 25 x scene-disjoint supply, scene-query retrieval minus type-agnostic static is <= +8 net. Falsified by >= +8 in that cell, meaning the residual comes from non-binding content of retrieved trajectories (e.g., a search heuristic) rather than the binding. P5 (the query matters only under demand) In relocated x 25 x fresh supply, scene-query minus goal-query retrieval is >= +8 net, and in canonical x 25 it is within +-8. Falsified by scene-query minus goal-query < +8 in the relocated cell (goal similarity already keys the sibling through class-scene correlation) or >= +8 in the canonical cell; both cells exist. P6 (compilability) In relocated x 25 x fresh supply, compiled table minus scene-query retrieval is >= -8 net. Falsified by table < retrieval - 8 in that cell, meaning the reader can use a 430-token trajectory but not a 3k-token table, so the query is necessary at 274 rows. Exploratory (declared, not confirmatory): whole-bank 80-item arm is <= scene-query retrieval - 8 (the sibling is not found among 80 items); falsified by whole-bank >= retrieval - 8 in the whole-bank cell. Stale-sibling supply gives retrieval <= type-agnostic static - 8; falsified by retrieval >= static - 8 in the stale cell.
Measurement and Noise Control: Primary outcome: task success on the same (game, seed) pairs across arms; nets in points; paired differences with a cluster bootstrap over games (1,000 resamples, seeds nested in games) giving 95% CIs; the +-8-net floor at 274 x 2 is the minimum reportable margin and all confirmatory margins (+14) exceed it; per-type differences (+-13 to +-15) are exploratory only. Fixed decoding temperature and seeds as in Measurement A; the same vLLM build, prompt template and retriever checkpoint in every arm; the static prefixes are byte-identical across episodes so prefix-cache hits are verified from the vLLM logs. Manipulation check precedes confirmatory cells; predictions and margins pre-registered in DESIGN.md before the first confirmatory cell. valid_seen and valid_unseen reported separately (unseen is the natural scene-disjoint supply), plus pooled. Prefill tokens per episode (cached/uncached) and wall-clock per episode logged for the accuracy-cost curve.

Name: protocol_bindings_procedure_count
Title: How Many Procedures Before a Cached Prompt Needs a Query: Planting Protocol-Keyed Procedures to Manipulate Procedure Count in ALFWorld
Short Hypothesis: The residual of experience retrieval over a type-agnostic cached prompt is a routing residual: it is positive only when the reader's in-context selection among the P procedures the task distribution spans is worse than the retriever's selection. ALFWorld spans P = 6 and shows no residual; multiplying P by planting protocol-keyed hidden preconditions (P = 6, 24, 96, 288) produces a residual above a threshold P*, and a factorized compiled prompt (six procedures plus one row per protocol) removes it again, so the property that makes a query necessary is the size of the smallest compiled form of the procedure set, not the number of procedures.
Related Work: Enrich-Retrieve-Rank (arXiv:2608.22695) shows in-context routing over a capability registry collapses as the registry grows, measured by Match@1 with one small router and no compiled-table control. SGR-Bench (arXiv:2605.22219) attributes search-agent failures to site-specific state configuration but does not test supplying procedures. Mem2ActBench (arXiv:2601.19935) shows memory frameworks fail to ground tool parameters without a no-memory or full-history baseline. WALL-E 2.0 (arXiv:2504.15785) learns environment rules as symbolic knowledge by alignment, without comparing retrieval against a compiled rule set at varying rule counts. Toolshed (arXiv:2410.14594), ScaleMCP (arXiv:2505.06416) and Graph RAG-Tool Fusion (arXiv:2502.07223) report tool-retrieval recall at scale, not task success against an all-tools prompt. Measurement C on this node supplies the six-procedure type-agnostic arm. Archived optimizer_substitutes_for_memory_scaffold could not separate scaffold from content; the oracle-routed arm here does.
Abstract: A bank of 1,465 ALFWorld trajectories contains at most six procedures, so a 400-token cached prompt listing all six is a complete substitute for retrieval and the retriever's only job, type identification, is done by the reader. We test whether a query becomes necessary once the number of distinct procedures grows, by planting procedures rather than naming them. A harness wrapper imposes protocols: each game announces a random protocol code in its first observation (for example 'Protocol K17 is in force'); protocol k adds one hidden precondition to one key action of the task procedure (examine the object before heating it, open and close the goal receptacle before putting, issue look at a receptacle before taking from it, and so on, drawn from a menu of (trigger action, prerequisite) pairs), and a violating action returns the standard 'Nothing happens.' The protocol's content is never described in the observation; it is learnable only from experience. Expert trajectories are regenerated by rule under each protocol and verified by replay, giving a bank in which the correct procedure is keyed by (type, protocol). The number of protocols R in {1, 4, 16, 48} sets P = 6R. Arms per level: k=0 (manipulation check), retrieval keyed by goal plus protocol line (k=3), an all-P compiled prompt (every (type, protocol) procedure, about 35 tokens each, up to about 10k cached tokens), a factorized compiled prompt (six procedures plus one row per protocol, at most 1.1k tokens), the six-procedure prompt with no protocol knowledge, an oracle-routed static arm holding only this game's (type, protocol) procedure (the routing-free upper bound), a length placebo (all-P prompt padded to 10k tokens at R = 4), and a whole-bank arm where the per-protocol bank fits. The prediction is a threshold in R between 4 and 48 for the all-P prompt, no threshold for the factorized prompt, and no residual over the oracle arm at any R; a Qwen3-8B ladder tests whether the threshold moves with the reader.
Experiments: 1. Wrapper: intercept env.step; maintain per-episode predicates (examined(o), opened-then-closed(r), looked(r), inventory-checked, visited(landmark)); if the action is the protocol's trigger and its prerequisite is unmet, return 'Nothing happens.' without state change; protocol code inserted into the first observation. Define 48 distinct protocols as (trigger in {take, put, heat, cool, clean, use, go to}, prerequisite in a menu of 8 distinct prior actions) minus incoherent pairs; assign codes uniformly to games at each R with a fixed seed. 2. Bank: for each train and eval game and each protocol in force, insert the prerequisite step into the expert action sequence by rule and replay through the wrapped environment; keep verified successes; the retriever indexes goal plus protocol line. 3. Manipulation check: k=0 on unmodified games vs k=0 under R = 1, 274 x 2 seeds; pre-registered escalation if the drop is < 8 net: violations count as episode failure instead of 'Nothing happens.' 4. Confirmatory ladder, each arm 274 x 2 seeds (~30 min): at R in {1, 4, 16, 48}: retrieval k=3, all-P compiled, factorized compiled, six-procedure no-protocol prompt, oracle-routed static; plus length placebo at R = 4 and whole-bank at R in {1, 4}. About 24 arms, ~13k episodes, ~11 h on two A100s. 5. Reader ladder (exploratory): Qwen3-8B on retrieval, all-P and factorized at R in {4, 16, 48}, ~4 h. 6. Compile source ablation: all-P and factorized prompts written by rule (exact by construction) vs written by Qwen3-32B from the bank, at R = 16. 7. Cost: cached vs uncached prefill tokens and wall-clock per episode; accuracy-cost curves per R; note that cached tokens still add per-step decode cost, so wall-clock is reported alongside tokens.
Baselines and Ablations: Static baselines (cached): all-P compiled prompt; factorized compiled prompt; six-procedure no-protocol prompt (knowledge-free control); oracle-routed single procedure (routing-free upper bound, non-deployable); length placebo (R = 4 content padded with 264 procedures from protocols not in force, matched to the R = 48 prompt length) to separate routing burden from context length; whole-bank arm at R in {1, 4} (all verified items for the game's type and protocol, <= 80 items). Retrieval: goal plus protocol-line query, k=3; ablations k=1, k=7 at R = 48; goal-only query at R = 48 (protocol code absent from the query) to show the query must carry the binding; random-protocol retrieval placebo at R = 48. Ordering ablation: all-P prompt sorted by protocol code vs shuffled. Second reader (Qwen3-8B) on the three main arms.

Falsified by a drop < 8 net (the reader discovers the precondition by trial within the budget); produced by the two k=0 cells; the pre-registered stricter wrapper is then used, and if the drop is still < 8 the study stops and reports the lever inert. P2 (no routing residual at low P) At R in {1, 4}, retrieval minus all-P compiled is <= +8 net. Falsified by a residual >= +8 at R = 4 (the reader already fails to route among 24 procedures), produced by the R = 4 retrieval and all-P cells. P3 (routing residual at high P) At R = 48, retrieval minus all-P compiled is >= +14 net, and the residual is non-decreasing in R. Falsified by < +8 net at R = 48 (the reader routes among 288 cached procedures as well as the retriever, so procedure count is not the property); produced by the R = 48 cells. P4 (not a context-length effect) At R = 4, the length placebo (10k-token prompt with 24 relevant procedures) is within +-8 of the unpadded all-P prompt. Falsified by placebo <= all-P - 8 (the degradation is length, not routing); produced by the placebo cell. P5 (factorization restores compilability) At R = 48, factorized compiled minus retrieval is >= -8 net. Falsified by factorized < retrieval - 8 (the reader cannot index 48 rows either, so the query is necessary at a row count of 48 and the property is table size, not procedure count); produced by the factorized cell at R = 48. P6 (residual is routing, not content) At every R, retrieval minus oracle-routed static is <= +8 net. Falsified by >= +8 at any R (retrieved trajectories carry value beyond the (type, protocol) procedure); produced by the oracle cells. P7 (exploratory, reader dependence) The smallest R with residual >= +14 is smaller for Qwen3-8B than for Qwen3-32B. Protocol assignment fixed per R by seed so every arm sees the same codes; codes are random strings so the reader cannot infer content; the wrapper is deterministic. Same decoding settings, vLLM build, prompt template and retriever as Measurement A. Prefix-cache hits verified from vLLM logs for all static arms; cached and uncached prefill tokens and wall-clock logged per episode.
