Name: cached_prefix_frontier
Title: Prefix Caching Moves the Break-Even: Measured Accuracy–GPU-Second Frontiers for Static, Whole-Bank and Retrieved Experience Prefixes in a Multi-Turn Agent
Short Hypothesis: In a multi-turn agent served with prefix caching, the cost of an experience prefix is set by how many distinct prefixes the arm emits across episodes and by how long the prefix is at decode time, not by its injected token count, so a matched-token budget mis-ranks the routes. Concretely: with caching off, an 80-item whole-bank prefix (~11k tokens) costs at least 3x the GPU-seconds per episode of k=3 retrieval (~430 tokens); with caching on it costs at most 1.5x, and k=3 retrieval costs at most 25% more than a type-conditioned static prompt because only the first turn's retrieved tokens are uncached. Retrieval from a small bank (24 or 80 items) keeps the accuracy of retrieval from the full 1,465-item bank while emitting few distinct prefixes, so retrieval's accuracy is available at static cost.
Related Work: 2603.04814 builds a cost model with prompt caching for Mem0 versus long context on conversational QA with one model; cost is modelled per turn, never measured inside an agent loop, and there is no compiled-static or whole-bank arm. AdaptiveScale (s2:62b577ec) and KVFlow (2507.07400) treat prefix-cache hit rate as a serving quantity with no task accuracy attached. InferScale (2607.27090) and HYPIC (2607.01299) make injected memory position-independently cacheable, engineering whose payoff is exactly the retrieval premium this idea measures. 2607.26497 finds retrieval crossovers on document corpora with one reader and no cost under caching; 2506.04301 reports agent compute scaling without a memory axis; Preping (2605.13880) claims 2-3x lower deployment cost for pre-built playbooks without separating caching from content; 2604.02596 shows BM25-selected shots beat many-shot on data efficiency in MT, not on serving cost. Archived memory_budget_confound (5.63) matched token budgets and treated tokens as the cost axis.
Abstract: Agent-memory papers count injected tokens as the cost of retrieval and treat a static prompt as free once cached; neither is what a serving stack charges. In a multi-turn agent every decode step re-reads the prefix through attention, a cached prefix still occupies KV memory that bounds batch size, and only the first turn of a retrieved prefix is uncached. We measure, rather than model, accuracy–GPU-second frontiers on ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B for three routes built from the same expert bank: compiled static prompts (type-agnostic and type-conditioned), the whole bank in context (24 and 80 items), and top-k retrieval from banks of 24, 80, 240 and 1,465 items. Each arm runs with vLLM prefix caching on and off on the same 274 games x 2 seeds as Measurements A and C, at a concurrency tuned to the serving queue on two A100s, with per-request uncached prefill, decode tokens and per-turn context length logged. We fit a three-term cost model (uncached prefill, decode tokens, decode x context length) and test it on a held-out arm. The predictions: caching reverses the cost ranking of whole-bank versus retrieval; the retrieval premium over a static prompt under caching is a first-turn effect below 25%; and retrieval from a small bank matches the full bank's accuracy while emitting few distinct prefixes. The output is a Pareto set per cache setting and a portable token-level accounting that replaces matched-token budgets.
Experiments: E0 (on disk, reused): Measurement A arms k=0, k=3, k=7 and Measurement C arms (type-conditioned 3 fixed exemplars; type-agnostic 6-procedure prompt) give accuracy on 274 games x 2 seeds. E1 new accuracy arms, 274 x 2 each: whole-bank-24 (4 items per type, ~3.4k tokens, one prefix), whole-bank-80 (13-14 per type, ~11k tokens, one prefix; truncation rule: stratified by type, shortest successful trajectories first), and BM25 goal retrieval k=3 from random type-stratified bank subsets of 24, 80 and 240 items; 2,740 episodes (~2.5 h). E2 cost runs: all nine arms x prefix caching {on, off} x ~270 episodes, arms interleaved in 3 blocks of 90 episodes, both GPUs, workers raised until each replica's running queue is at least 8; log per request prompt_tokens, cached_tokens, completion_tokens and per-turn context length from the vLLM usage fields, wall-clock per block and nvidia-smi utilization every 10 s; GPU-seconds per episode = 2 x wall-clock / episodes at saturated queue; 4,860 episodes (~4 h). E3 fit GPU-s = a x uncached_prefill + b x decode_tokens + c x sum over decode steps of context length on eight arms and predict the ninth (whole-bank-24). E4 frontier: success from E0/E1 against GPU-s per episode from E2 for both routes under both cache settings; Pareto set per setting; additional concurrency ladder (8/16/32 workers per replica) on whole-bank-80 and k=3, cost only, to expose KV-occupancy effects. Positive controls: (i) the caching toggle must cut the type-agnostic static arm's uncached prefill tokens by at least 5x, otherwise the cache is not functioning and no cost claim is made; (ii) k=3 accuracy under cache on versus off must agree within the ±8 floor, otherwise cost and accuracy cannot be paired.
Baselines and Ablations: Baselines (static arms first, per the brief): k=0; type-agnostic 6-procedure prompt (1 distinct prefix); type-conditioned 3 fixed exemplars (6 distinct prefixes); whole-bank-24 and whole-bank-80 (1 prefix each). Retrieval route: BM25 goal retrieval k=3 from 24, 80, 240 and 1,465 items (distinct prefixes rising toward C(n_type,3)); k=7 from 1,465. Ablations: caching on/off (cost only); concurrency 8/16/32 per replica (cost only); retrieved items ordered canonically by item id so identical sets share a prefix versus ordered by score (cost only); whole-bank-80 item order type-blocked versus shuffled (accuracy, exploratory).
Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (headline, cost-ranking reversal): with caching off, whole-bank-80 costs at least 3x the GPU-s per episode of k=3 retrieval; with caching on, at most 1.5x. Falsified by whole-bank-80 at or above 2x k=3 with caching on (decode attention over an 11k context and KV occupancy dominate, or the shared prefix is evicted under concurrency), produced by the whole-bank-80 versus k=3 cells of E2 under cache on; or by a cache-off ratio below 2, produced by the same pair under cache off. P2: with caching on, k=3 retrieval costs at most 25% more GPU-s per episode than the type-conditioned 3-exemplar static arm. Falsified by a premium at or above 50%, produced by the k=3 versus 3-fixed-exemplar cells under cache on (first-turn prefill dominance or per-turn cache misses would produce it). P3: whole-bank-80 success is within ±8 net of k=3 retrieval on both splits. Falsified by whole-bank-80 at least 8 net below k=3 (many-shot distraction), produced by the whole-bank-80 arm of E1; not entailed, since containing the items does not make the reader use them. P4: retrieval-from-24 and retrieval-from-80 are within ±8 net of retrieval-from-1,465 while their uncached prefill tokens under caching are at most 30% of the full-bank arm's. Falsified by success at least 8 net lower at 24 or 80 (item specificity matters), produced by the bank-size ladder of E1; or by a cache-hit fraction at or below 50% at bank 24 (prefix diversity from set/order variation), produced by that arm's cached_tokens logs. P5: the three-term cost model predicts the held-out whole-bank-24 arm's GPU-s per episode within 25%. Falsified by held-out error above 25%, produced by E3.
Measurement and Noise Control: Accuracy: paired (game, seed) cells with A and C on 274 x 2; ±8 net floor for arm-versus-arm claims; margins stated as fractions of the Gate-0 gain (+27/+32 net at k=3): the ±8 in P3/P4 is 25-30% of that gain; per-type numbers exploratory. Cost: GPU-s per episode from wall-clock at saturated queue in 3 interleaved blocks per arm per cache setting, median and bootstrap CI over blocks; token quantities from per-request vLLM usage fields; utilization and throughput (episodes/min, tok/s per GPU) reported per arm; ratios in P1/P2 computed on block medians with CIs from 1,000 bootstrap resamples of episodes, and a prediction counts as confirmed only if its CI excludes the falsifying value. Cost-model fit reports R-squared and held-out error. Pre-registration of arms, truncation rule, concurrency and floors before E1.

No paper measures a cache-toggle cost reversal between whole-bank and retrieved prefixes in an agent loop.
Risk Factors and Limitations: KV memory on an 80GB A100 with a 32B reader may evict the 11k shared prefix under high concurrency, turning the whole-bank arm into an uncached arm; this is a real outcome (it falsifies P1) but node-specific, so the KV budget and the concurrency at which eviction starts are reported. vLLM prefix caching is position-dependent; item-level position-independent KV reuse (InferScale-style) would shrink the retrieval premium further and is stated as the implication, not measured. GPU-seconds depend on the serving stack; the token-level accounting is portable, the fitted coefficients are not. ALFWorld's 140-token items let 80 fit in 16k; environments with 1k-token items hit the whole-bank ceiling at 16 items. One reader; the crossover-moves-with-reader question is left to a second backbone.
Addresses gap: G25 (accuracy-cost curves under prompt caching untested) and G21 (no same-budget whole-bank control).
Not a restatement of: Brief bullet 'Cost: a static prefix is prefix-cached by vLLM; retrieval injects a different prefix per episode, so the token cost difference is measurable': the brief treats injected token count as the cost; this idea claims token counts mis-rank the routes because a cached prefix is still paid at every decode step and occupies KV, and it manipulates caching to show the ranking reversal. Nearest digest card 2603.04814: models caching cost for single-turn QA; this idea claims the agent loop changes the accounting (only first-turn retrieved tokens are uncached, the static prefix is paid at decode) and measures it with whole-bank and compiled arms. Archived memory_budget_confound (5.63): matched token budgets; this idea claims matched tokens is the wrong cost axis under caching.

Name: exemplar_lottery
Title: The Exemplar Lottery: Retrieval's Gain Over a Fixed Prompt Is a Quantile of the Static Arm's Draw Distribution, Not a Mean Shift
Short Hypothesis: A fixed exemplar prompt is one draw from the bank, and reported retrieval gains are measured against a single draw. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B, the success of a type-conditioned three-exemplar fixed prompt varies across random draws from the same expert bank by more than the mean gap between retrieval and the fixed arm; retrieval sits at the upper quantile of that draw distribution, does not beat the best held-out draw by more than the noise floor, and a one-time length rule (shortest successful trajectories per type) recovers it without a query. Retrieval's value on a template environment is selection robustness, and it has to be reported against the draw distribution with its spread.
Related Work: Traj-Bootstrap (2505.00234, NeurIPS 2025) grows a self-generated example database on ALFWorld and other tasks, notices that equal-size databases differ in quality, and picks the best by population-based selection plus exemplar-level curation; it always retrieves and never compares to a fixed no-retriever draw, so the variance it exploits is never attributed to exemplar choice versus retrieval. Classic ICL sensitivity work (calibrate-before-use, prompt-order sensitivity, kNN demonstration selection beating random) measured the spread of random demonstration draws on classification and showed retrieval beats the random mean, not the random maximum or a curated fixed set, and never on multi-turn agent trajectories. 2512.04106 (retrieved few-shot beats random few-shot on vulnerability detection, one model, no curated fixed set) and 2406.14596 ICAL (retrieved insight exemplars, no fixed-set test) report one static comparison each. SkillEvolBench (2605.24117) calls skill gains unstable without decomposing the instability. Measurement C on this node runs one draw per static arm. Archived decorative_retriever (5.75) observed retrieval-set overlap.
Abstract: Every static exemplar prompt is a draw from the bank, and the reported gain of retrieval over it is measured against one draw. We ask what the distribution of that draw looks like and where retrieval sits in it. On ALFWorld with Qwen3-32B we run 16 random draws of a type-conditioned three-exemplar prompt from the expert bank, 8 draws from the self pool, and, for 8 random 80-item bank samples, both a fixed draw and k=3 retrieval from the same sample, all paired on the 274 games x 2 seeds of Measurement A; we add three one-time curation rules (shortest trajectories, retriever-embedding medoids, longest trajectories) that select exemplars without a query. We decompose the fixed arm's variance into draw, seed and game components and locate retrieval's success in the draw distribution, selecting the best draw on a held-out split to avoid the winner's curse. The claim is that retrieval's gain over a fixed prompt on a template environment is the spread of the exemplar lottery, not a mean shift. If instead the draws cluster and retrieval exceeds the best held-out draw by more than the floor, retrieval carries per-instance information that no fixed prompt has. Either outcome fixes how retrieval gains should be reported: against the draw distribution, with its spread, and with the cheapest curation rule as the static arm.
Experiments: E0 (on disk): A (k=0; k=3 BM25 retrieval from the full expert bank, R_full) and C (one fixed draw, reported later as its quantile in the lottery). E1: F_1..F_16, type-conditioned fixed prompts, each a uniform draw of 3 successful expert trajectories per type from the full bank, same slot and format as C's fixed arm, token-matched to k=3 (~430 tokens); 274 x 2 each, 8,768 episodes (~7.3 h). E2: S_1..S_8, the same from the self pool (on-policy detours); 4,384 episodes (~3.7 h). E3: 8 random type-stratified 80-item bank samples; for each, F_b (fixed draw of 3 per type from the sample) and R_b (k=3 BM25 retrieval from the sample), paired; 8,768 episodes (~7.3 h). E4: curation arms C_short (3 shortest successful trajectories per type), C_medoid (per-type medoids under the retriever's own representation), C_worst (3 longest per type, negative control); 1,644 episodes (~1.4 h). E5: held-out best-draw selection: choose the best of F_1..16 on seed 1 x valid_seen and compare to R_full on seed 2 x valid_unseen, and the mirror. E6: variance decomposition: crossed random-effects logistic model with game, draw and draw x seed intercepts; simple SDs of arm-level net scores across draws and across seeds reported alongside; bootstrap over games. Static arms are prefix-cached and retrieval arms are not; uncached prefill tokens per episode logged for every arm as a secondary cost axis. Total ~23.6k episodes (~20 h on two A100s), pre-registered draw seeds.
Baselines and Ablations: Baselines: k=0; R_full (retrieval k=3 from 1,465 items); the 16 expert draws and 8 self-pool draws as the static-arm distribution; the 8 paired (F_b, R_b) bank samples; C's single draw located as a quantile. Curation arms as one-time static alternatives: C_short, C_medoid, C_worst. Ablations: draws restricted to scene-disjoint items for each test game (removes near-duplicate luck from the lottery); single-exemplar draws token-matched to k=1 for 8 draws if budget allows; the self-pool draws with detour steps removed by rule (tests whether the wider spread, if found, is from detours or from selection).
Falsifiable Predictions: P1 (headline): the SD across the 16 expert draws of net success is at least 2x the within-draw seed SD, and the draw range (max minus min) is at least the mean gap R_full minus mean(F_d). Falsified by draw SD at or below seed SD, or a range below half the mean gap, produced by the F_1..16 arm if draws cluster (a live outcome, since expert trajectories within a type share the procedure). P2: R_full does not exceed the held-out best draw by more than 8 net. Falsified by R_full minus F_best-heldout above 8 net (retrieval carries per-instance information beyond exemplar choice), produced by E5. P3: self-pool draws have SD at least 1.5x the expert draws' SD and a mean at least 8 net lower. Falsified by SD_self at or below SD_expert, produced by E2 (self-pool successes are procedurally equivalent despite detours). P4: C_short lands within ±8 net of R_full and C_worst lands at least 8 net below R_full. Falsified by C_short at least 8 net below R_full (a cheap rule does not recover retrieval's selection), produced by E4; or by C_worst within ±8 of R_full (exemplar choice does not matter, which also removes P1's premise), produced by E4. P5: over the 8 bank samples the paired residual R_b minus F_b has mean within ±8 net and an across-sample SD larger than its across-seed SD. Falsified by a mean residual above 8 net (retrieval beats a same-bank fixed draw on average), produced by E3.
Measurement and Noise Control: All arms on the 274 x 2 (game, seed) grid of A, so every comparison is paired; ±8 net floor for arm-versus-arm claims and margins of 25-30% of the Gate-0 gain (+27/+32). Draw SD is estimated over 16 arm-level net scores, each on 548 episodes (per-draw SE about 2 net), so a draw SD of 4 net is distinguishable from the seed SD estimated from the 16 paired seed differences; the chi-square CI on an SD from 16 draws is about ±35%, hence the 2x ratio in P1. Range and quantile statements carry bootstrap CIs from 1,000 resamples of games drawn jointly across arms to preserve pairing. The held-out selection in E5 removes the winner's curse from best-draw comparisons. Per-type spreads are exploratory. Pre-registration lists draw seeds, bank-sample seeds, curation rules and floors before any run.

Name: state_key_pays_only_for_planted_bindings
Title: What the Query Can Index: Observation-Keyed Retrieval Beats Goal-Keyed Retrieval and the Best Static Prompt Only When the Bank Carries Scene-Keyed Bindings at a Controlled Rate
Short Hypothesis: The residual of experience retrieval over the best static prompt equals the within-type variance in the bank that the query key can index and a fixed prompt cannot. On ALFWorld the goal sentence already reveals type and object class, so a goal-keyed retriever cannot index anything a type-conditioned static prompt lacks, whereas an observation-keyed retriever can index scene identity. We plant scene-keyed bindings (where the target object is in this scene) into the bank for 0/25/50/100 percent of evaluation games and predict: every key's residual is inside the +/-8-net floor at 0 percent; the residual rises with the rate for the observation key only; a compact whole-binding table in a cached static prompt matches observation-keyed retrieval at 100 percent; and a wrong planted binding costs more than a right one gains.
Related Work: Synapse (arXiv:2306.07863) keys trajectory exemplars by abstracted state but never compares the state key against a goal key or a matched-length static prompt and does not manipulate whether the bank holds state-keyed content. FocusMem (arXiv:2608.04530) adds state-conditioned retrieval with a trust gate for GUI agents with the same omissions. RAP (arXiv:2402.03610) retrieves by current situation with no static or goal-keyed control. arXiv:2603.18272 trains the reader (LoRA) to use retrieved trajectories with a fixed goal query and no random or fixed control. ICAL (arXiv:2406.14596) reports no fixed-set control. Measurement A on this node found unseen ~ seen, i.e. no scene component in the retrieved value; this proposal manufactures that component at four rates. Archived compile_dont_retrieve (6.0) called the query-conditioned read inert without manipulating the property that would make it non-inert; decorative_retriever (5.75) observed overlap only. Cross-axis: arXiv:2607.10608 (compliance) motivates the wrong-binding arm; arXiv:2603.04814 and arXiv:2506.03989 motivate the cached whole-table arm.
Abstract: Agent-memory papers report the gain of a retriever over no memory, rarely over a fixed prompt built from the same experience, and never as a function of what the query key can index. We formalise the retrieval residual as the within-type variance of the bank that is indexable by the key but not by a static prompt, and test it on ALFWorld (Qwen3-32B, 274 games x 2 seeds per cell, k=3, token-matched to +/-5 percent) by crossing three keys (goal sentence, initial observation, current observation at first stall) with a bank in which scene-keyed binding items ('scene signature S: object O was found in receptacle R', ~30 tokens, derived from the game's PDDL) are planted for r in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0} of evaluation games, fixed per game across seeds and keys; a natural-binding level built from same-floorplan train trajectories, whose correctness rate is measured, and a wrong-binding level (100 percent incorrect receptacle) complete the ladder. Baselines are the best type-conditioned static arm and the type-agnostic static arm from Measurement C (re-run on the same seeds for test-retest), random-within-type selection at matched length, a whole-binding-table static prompt (all 274 rows, ~8k tokens, one cached prefix for the arm) at r=0.5 and 1.0, and oracle injection of the game's own binding as the positive control. Prefill tokens per episode are logged per arm so cached static prefixes and uncached retrieved prefixes give an accuracy-cost frontier. Predictions: at r=0 no key exceeds the best static arm by more than 8 net; the observation-key residual rises with r to at least half the Gate-0 gain at r=1.0 while the goal-key residual stays inside the floor; the cached whole-table prompt matches observation-keyed retrieval; and the wrong-binding harm exceeds the right-binding gain. The result is a pre-registered rule for when a query is necessary: only when a bank statistic (variance within type that the key can index) is non-zero, and the amount is measured rather than named.
Experiments: Setting: ALFWorld valid_seen and valid_unseen (274 games), 2 seeds, identical seeds across arms; Qwen3-32B on two vLLM replicas (one per GPU, prefix caching on); k=3 (~430 tokens); a planted binding item replaces the same number of exemplar tokens so all arms are matched to +/-5 percent (verified from logged prefill counts). Bank manipulation: binding item = 'Scene signature <sorted receptacle inventory of the first observation>: <object class> was found in <receptacle>' (~30 tokens); planted from the game's PDDL for a random fraction r in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0} of games (assignment fixed per game across seeds and keys); natural level = same-floorplan train-split expert trajectories with their measured correctness rate p_nat (a fifth, uncontrolled rate); wrong level = plausible but incorrect receptacle for 100 percent of games. Query manipulation: goal key (goal sentence; BM25 and bge-m3 dense, index over trajectories plus binding items), initial-observation key (first observation text), stall key (current observation at the first repeated or 'Nothing happens' action, retrieved items appended as a new message so the cached prefix survives), random-within-type at matched length. Static arms: best type-conditioned static (3 fixed exemplars + procedure) and type-agnostic static (six procedures) from Measurement C, re-run; whole-binding-table static (type-agnostic prompt + all 274 rows, ~8k tokens, one cached prefix) at r=0.5 (137 true rows, the reader must find its row or ignore the table) and r=1.0. Positive control: oracle injection of the game's own binding. Cells: 3 keys x 4 rates (12) + random x {0, 1.0} (2) + wrong-binding x {goal, observation} (2) + whole-table x 2 + oracle (1) + natural x {goal, observation} (2) + 2 static re-runs = 23 cells, ~30 min each, ~6 h wall-clock with both GPUs saturated (episode workers tuned to the vLLM running queue >= 8 per replica). Order (pre-registered): static re-runs and oracle first (test-retest floor and positive control), then the rate ladder for the observation key, then the goal and stall keys, then wrong and natural levels. Cost: uncached prefill tokens per episode and cache hit rate per arm from vLLM logs; report accuracy vs uncached tokens. Ablations: scene signature as receptacle-inventory hash vs raw first-observation text; k=1 vs k=3 for the observation key at r=1.0; Qwen3-8B reader on the r=1.0 cells (exploratory). WebShop is out of scope for this claim (no scene structure); the bank statistic proposed for prediction is the fraction of items whose content varies within type conditional on the key.
Baselines and Ablations: Baselines: best type-conditioned static arm and type-agnostic static arm (Measurement C, re-run on the same seeds); goal-keyed top-3 retrieval (Measurement A, re-run at r=0); random-within-type at matched length (separates the retriever from having type-relevant content); whole-binding-table cached static prompt (the whole-bank arm for the compact binding sub-bank); oracle binding injection (upper bound). Ablations: key encoder (BM25 vs bge-m3) for the goal and observation keys; scene-signature form; k=1 vs k=3 at r=1.0; stall key vs initial-observation key at r=1.0 (does timing of the state matter when the binding is scene-level); reader size (Qwen3-8B, exploratory); natural vs planted binding at the same measured correctness rate (realism check).
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (rate-0 residual): at r=0 each key (goal, initial observation, stall) minus the best static arm lies within +/-8 net on the pooled 274x2 cell. Falsified if any key exceeds the best static arm by more than +8 net at r=0. Arm: the three r=0 retrieval cells against the re-run best static cell; nothing in the design prevents the object-specific exemplars they retrieve from adding success, which is what Measurement C's residual tests, so the outcome is open.
- P2 (key x rate interaction): the observation-key residual over the best static arm rises monotonically with r and reaches at least +13 net (half the Gate-0 gain) at r=1.0; the goal-key residual stays within +/-8 net at every r. Falsified if (a) the observation-key residual at r=1.0 is below +8 net (the key does not index the scene or the reader does not apply the binding), or (b) the goal-key residual at r=1.0 exceeds +8 net (object-class matching alone selects the right scene's row often enough). Arms: observation-key and goal-key cells at r=1.0 and the trend across r=0.25/0.5.
- P3 (whole table vs retrieval): at r=1.0 the whole-binding-table static arm (274 rows, cached) is within +/-8 net of observation-keyed retrieval, and at r=0.5 it is within +/-8 net of observation-keyed retrieval at r=0.5. Falsified if the table arm is below the retrieval arm by more than 8 net at either rate (the reader cannot locate its row among 274, or the 137 rows for other scenes at r=0.5 induce compliance). Arm: the two whole-table cells. Not entailed: the table contains the retrieved row, but whether an 8k-token table lies inside the reader's effective context is empirical and can come out either way.

Name: rank_flat_retriever_is_a_type_classifier
Title: Rank-Flat Retrieval: Within-Type Similarity Rank and Near-Duplicate Removal Do Not Move Task Success, So the Experience Retriever Reduces to a Type Classifier Plus a Similarity-Scaled Compliance Hazard
Short Hypothesis: On trajectory banks the retriever's contribution to task success is a step function of type match: replacing the top-3 items with items at within-type similarity rank 10-12 or 50-52, or removing every bank item that shares the test game's (type, object, receptacle) or (type, object), changes success by less than the +/-8-net floor, while removing the type drops success to the wrong-type placebo. On the harm side, the most similar wrong-type item hurts more than a random wrong-type item, and the harm is content-driven: relabelling the same items as retrieved memory, examples or instructions changes nothing, whereas an explicit mismatch warning reduces it. A per-type cached sub-bank of up to 80 items therefore matches top-3 retrieval at lower uncached cost.
Related Work: KATE (Liu et al. 2021) and EPR (Rubin et al. 2021) established kNN demonstration selection over random for classification and generation; Rank-ICL (ICTIR 2026) finds ranking-based selection beneficial but not uniformly superior to random; CoDR (arXiv:2511.08977) and gradient-matching selection (arXiv:2506.04579) optimise selection without a within-class rank ladder; arXiv:2512.04106 reports retrieved > random on one model and task with no fixed set. ExpeL (arXiv:2308.10144) retrieves successful trajectories by task similarity on ALFWorld with no rank or leave-out ladder; ExpGraph (arXiv:2605.30712) ranks by utility with no matched random control; arXiv:2603.02473 finds retrieval dominates write on LoCoMo by recall, not action; arXiv:2505.15561 finds passage order no better than shuffling. The compliance trap (arXiv:2607.10608) shows conflicting memory is adopted at the first decision point but does not vary the wrong item's similarity or framing and does not measure the symmetric benefit at matched length; ReMem (arXiv:2511.20857) leaves near-duplicate dependence untested. Archived decorative_retriever (5.75) observed retrieval-set overlap; order_randomized_leakage_audit (5.7) observed leakage; neither manipulated it.
Abstract: If the value of experience retrieval on a template environment is the type's procedure, the retriever is a type classifier and everything it does beyond that is decorative or harmful. We test this on ALFWorld (Qwen3-32B, 274 games x 2 seeds, k=3, token-matched to +/-5 percent) with two manipulations of what the retriever returns and one of what the bank contains. The rank ladder replaces the top-3 items with items at within-type bge-m3 similarity rank 10-12, 50-52 and random-within-type. The leave-out ladder rebuilds the index per game after removing items sharing the game's (type, object class, target receptacle), (type, object class), or type, which manipulates near-duplicate availability directly rather than observing it. The harm arms present the most similar wrong-type item (e.g. a heat trajectory for a cool task) against Measurement C's random wrong-type placebo, and present the same wrong items under four headers ('Examples', 'Retrieved from memory of similar past tasks', 'Instructions: follow this procedure', and a mismatch warning) to separate content from framing, with the warning as the positive control that framing can move compliance. A per-type cached sub-bank (all items of the type up to 80, ~11k tokens, six cached prefixes) tests whether a classifier plus a static prefix replaces the retriever entirely. All retrieval cells are reported as differences from the best static arm of Measurement C; retriever metrics (same-object recall, mean similarity) are logged as secondary outcomes to show they move while success does not. Predictions: rank 50-52 is within the floor of rank 1-3; leave-out levels 1 and 2 are within the floor; level 3 falls to the placebo; the most similar wrong item hurts by more than 8 net over the random wrong item; headers do not move success but the warning does; and the cached sub-bank matches top-3. Together these give a measured statement of what an experience retriever is for on a template environment and where its hazard lies.
Experiments: Setting as in Measurement A/C: 274 games x 2 seeds, identical seeds across arms, Qwen3-32B on two vLLM replicas with prefix caching, k=3 (~430 tokens), items length-matched within +/-5 percent by choosing the nearest-length item inside each rank window. Rank ladder (type-conditioned retrieval, type read from the goal sentence as in Measurement A): ranks 1-3 (Measurement A re-run), 10-12, 50-52, random-within-type; a type-agnostic variant of the top-3 cell retrieves from the whole bank without the type filter. Leave-out ladder: per test game, remove bank items sharing (type, object class id, target receptacle id) [L1], (type, object class id) [L2], type [L3], then retrieve top-3 from the remainder; ALFWorld object class ids are used so synonyms do not leak. Harm arms: most-similar wrong-type items (nearest neighbours among other-type items by bge-m3 similarity to the goal) vs Measurement C's random wrong-type fixed exemplar (re-run); framing cells present the most-similar wrong-type items under 'Examples', 'Retrieved from memory of similar past tasks', 'Instructions: follow this procedure', and 'Examples (may be from a different task; follow only if the task matches)'. Whole-type sub-bank: all items of the game's type up to 80 (truncation rule: shortest first), one cached prefix per type. Static baselines: best type-conditioned static and type-agnostic static from Measurement C, re-run. Cells: rank ladder 4 + type-agnostic top-3 1 + leave-out 3 + harm 2 + framing 3 (the 'Examples' header is the similar-wrong cell) + sub-bank 1 + static re-runs 2 = 16 cells, ~30 min each, ~4 h with both GPUs busy. Secondary outcomes per cell: same-object recall, same-receptacle recall, mean similarity of returned items. Cost: uncached prefill tokens per episode per arm; the sub-bank arm's cache hit rate is verified. Order (pre-registered): static and A re-runs first (test-retest), then harm and warning arms (positive controls), then ladders and sub-bank. Per-type availability of rank-50 items is reported; for types with fewer than 55 items the deepest available rank window is used and declared.
Baselines and Ablations: Baselines: best type-conditioned static arm and type-agnostic static arm (Measurement C re-runs); top-3 goal-keyed retrieval (Measurement A re-run); random-within-type at matched length; random wrong-type placebo (Measurement C, re-run). Ablations: type-conditioned vs type-agnostic top-3 (is the type filter doing the work); rank window 10-12 vs 50-52; leave-out L1 vs L2 vs L3; similar-wrong vs random-wrong; four framing headers; sub-bank at 40 vs 80 items (exploratory); BM25 vs bge-m3 for the rank ladder (exploratory).
Falsifiable Predictions:
- P1 (rank-flat): rank 50-52 within type is within +/-8 net of rank 1-3 on the pooled 274x2 cell. Falsified if rank 1-3 exceeds rank 50-52 by more than 8 net. Arm: the rank-50 cell against the rank-1 re-run. Not entailed: rank within a type varies object and receptacle match, which can carry success.
- P2 (near-duplicate independence): leave-out levels L1 and L2 each change success by less than 8 net relative to the full-bank top-3 cell. Falsified if either drops success by 8 net or more (the gain is carried by near-duplicates). Arm: L1 and L2 cells.
- P3 (type removal): L3 falls to within +/-8 net of the random wrong-type placebo. Falsified if L3 stays more than 8 net above the placebo (cross-type procedure transfers, e.g. heat to cool). Arm: L3 cell against the placebo re-run.
- P4 (similarity-scaled harm): the most-similar wrong-type arm is below the random wrong-type placebo by more than 8 net. Falsified if the difference is below 8 net (compliance does not scale with similarity). Arm: the similar-wrong ('Examples' header) cell against the placebo re-run.
- P5 (framing null with positive control): the 'Retrieved from memory' and 'Instructions' headers are within +/-8 net of the 'Examples' header, while the mismatch-warning header raises success by 8 net or more over 'Examples'. Falsified if either header shifts success by 8 net or more (framing drives compliance), or if the warning fails to shift it (then the null is uninterpretable and is reported as such). Arms: the three framing cells against the 'Examples' cell.
- P6 (per-type cached sub-bank): the whole-type sub-bank (up to 80 items, cached) is within +/-8 net of rank 1-3 with lower uncached prefill per episode. Falsified if it is below rank 1-3 by more than 8 net (many-shot degradation at ~11k tokens). Arm: the sub-bank cell. Not entailed: the sub-bank contains the top-3 items, but whether 80 trajectories inside the reader's context preserve their use is empirical.
- P7 (type filter is the retriever): type-agnostic top-3 retrieval from the whole bank is within +/-8 net of type-conditioned top-3. Falsified if the type-agnostic cell is below the type-conditioned cell by more than 8 net (similarity over the whole bank returns wrong-type items often enough to trigger P4's harm). Arm: the type-agnostic top-3 cell.
Measurement and Noise Control: Paired (game, seed) cells with identical seeds; primary outcome task success; every retrieval cell is also reported as its difference from the best static arm so rank-flatness is anchored to the residual over static; net differences with cluster-bootstrap CIs over games (2,000 resamples); +/-8-net floor pre-registered, margins as fractions of the Gate-0 gain (+27/+32); per-type numbers exploratory (+/-13-15). Test-retest from the static and A re-runs. Secondary retriever metrics (same-object recall, mean similarity) are reported next to success for every cell so a flat success curve over a steep metric curve is visible. Token matching within +/-5 percent verified from logged prefill counts; item selection inside rank windows is length-matched, not similarity-matched. Positive controls (A's gain over static; P4's harm; P5's warning) must clear the floor before P1, P2 or P5 nulls are interpreted.
